measurement_vs_inference.rule: A measurement and the conclusion drawn from it are TWO statements, and this file must keep them apart. Record what was run and what it printed; record separately what you concluded, and name the steps between. A conclusion written as if it were the measurement is inherited by the next pass as measured fact.
measurement_vs_inference.why_this_block_exists: The previous HANDOFF said, citing a live run, that the agent holds the store's exclusive flock for its whole life and therefore `hop nodes` refuses while the tunnel is up. The run was real and still reproduces: `flock -x <root>/.lock sleep 8 &` then `hop nodes` → exit 1 after 5043 ms. The conclusion was wrong, and two inference steps did the damage: (1) 'the agent holds the store' → 'the agent holds the lock' — `store.Open` takes no lock, `load()` reads all three files without one, and the lock lives inside `transact`, per transaction (measured: 559 transactions, mean 1.05 ms); (2) 'the lock is held' → 'a reader waits' — a reader takes no lock at all. Both steps were invisible because the sentence read like a measurement.

closed_this_pass.measured_before_deciding: The reported defect reproduces and the numbers are the pass's own, not inherited: cmd/hop/measure_test.go, TestS47MeasureSweepLockUnderALiveWriter — writer without pauses, 40 real `hop nodes`, five runs, worst of forty 457 ms · 806 · 808 · 1.961 s · 2.063 s against a median of 4 ms. An OUTLIER, not a slowdown: only the Open that lands in the temp-file window pays. Control that separates it from the scheduler: the same run under HOP_DISABLE=atomic_write (no temp files at all) — worst 7 ms, before the fix.
closed_this_pass.second_half_the_task_did_not_name: The writer paid too, and by a mechanism worth keeping: its worst Flush was 51 ms in ALL FIVE runs — that is lockRetry (50 ms) plus the write, i.e. one full poll round lost to a reader that had gone sweeping. After the fix: 1.1–1.5 ms. So the lock taken for the sweep cost both sides.
closed_this_pass.shape: The conservative option the finding pass named: the sweep TRIES the lock (Store.tryTransact, internal/store/store.go) and skips when it is busy — a busy lock IS the proof that the temp file's owner is alive. The rejected alternative ('check for garbage after the lock') fixes nothing: it makes the check exact while the reader still WAITS, and the whole latency is the wait. The missing-files branch still waits, deliberately: that is a write, not a sweep, and it happens once per store directory (§6.14).
closed_this_pass.after: `hop nodes` worst 6 ms, writer's worst Flush 1.1 ms. W65's own measure also fell from 56 ms to 6 ms.
closed_this_pass.guard_and_controls: S47 — TestS47OpenDoesNotWaitForTheSweepLock (internal/store/lock_test.go), registry row in docs/verification-store.md §5.4. The second store opens with the fake clock STOPPED: lock waiting runs on that clock, so 'waited' means 'never returned', and the red shows up in two real seconds instead of the go test timeout. Three manual negative controls, each reddening a different half with its own message: transact instead of tryTransact ('Open ждёт замок ради уборки'); sweep with no lock at all ('Open снёс временный файл идущей чужой записи'); no sweep ever ('мусор пережил Open со свободным замком', and S26 with it).

next_task.name: `hop up` внутри окна orphaned отказывает состоянием, а не смыслом
next_task.why_first: It is the only item that is a defect rather than a platform or an installer, it is small in code, and §5.6 is explicit that a refusal must say what it is: the user is currently shown a state-machine sentence about a phase they have no verb to observe or to clear.
next_task.first_step_is_a_measurement: NOT reproduced by the controller — the mechanism was confirmed by reading only (see measurement_vs_inference at the top). Reproduce it before designing anything: internal/l3 now hands every agent its own -client-socket and its own HOP_STORE, so a stand test can kill the agent with the tunnel up (Detach, not Stop — the interface is meant to survive, T24), start a fresh agent with a fresh token, and run `hop up` inside the orphan deadline.
next_task.mechanism_read_not_measured: cmd/hop/transport.go `acquire` tries Attach by token first and falls back to `Start` (§6.2, T24). internal/tunnel/tunnel.go:215 lets Attach in only from Orphaned; Start refuses unless the phase is down. So the failure needs BOTH halves: the reattach lost its token (a fresh token file, e.g. what the L3 stand hands each agent) AND the tunnel is still inside its orphan deadline. Once orphan_deadline expires the tunnel is torn down and Start works again.
next_task.what: Kill the agent while the tunnel is up, without `hop down` (Detach, not Stop — the interface is meant to survive, T24). The next `hop up` fails with `tunnel: операция недопустима в текущем состоянии: orphaned, ожидалось down`.
next_task.the_decision_is_the_task: The user is shown a state-machine sentence about a phase they have no verb to observe or clear. §5.6 requires a refusal to say what it is: within the orphan window with the token gone, the honest answer names the deadline and offers the way out, and the way out has to exist. Decide whether `hop up` should wait out the deadline, whether a verb should drop an orphan deliberately, or whether the token should be recoverable — that decision is the task.
next_task.size: small in code, and the whole of it is the decision

notes.doclint: Fast. CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 48 policies as of this pass, ~25-35 min wall clock — expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. There is no per-policy selection: for a per-task gate run the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name> by hand; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). No root needed — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN in a fresh netns. Reuse the built binary across runs. WITHOUT -test.v the package prints only a final PASS, and a fully-skipped package prints the same PASS: count `--- PASS` lines (19 as of this pass, zero SKIP) before believing it ran. Name what unshare does NOT isolate: $HOME (hence per-test HOP_STORE) and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (hence per-test -client-socket).
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). realtimelint is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. gofmt -l ./internal reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code. Capture the baseline before starting — it makes acceptance a diff instead of a judgement.

notes.what_is_not_a_flake: cmd/hop/measure_test.go compares against time in exactly one place — `hop nodes` must return 0 — and the margin there is three orders of magnitude. A refusal in that test is a regression, not load. The 'longest held' numbers it logs are not assertions and move freely on a busy machine.
